entities.summary: Wang Chaji was a Korean politician, general, and ambassador during the Goryeo period. He was born in unknown year and died on March 30, 1122. Chaji was the deputy of military commander Yun Kwan and trained seventeen-thousand Jurchen soldiers from 1100 to 1108. His military campaigns expanded the Goryeo Empire's borders and strengthened its alliances with neighboring states. Chaji's diplomatic efforts also helped to secure trade agreements and cultural exchanges with China and Japan. As a key figure in the Goryeo court, Chaji played a crucial role in shaping the empire's foreign policy and military strategies. His legacy as a skilled military commander and diplomat has endured for centuries, with many historians praising his strategic genius and diplomatic acumen. Chaji's contributions to the Goryeo Empire's expansion and modernization have left a lasting impact on Korean history and continue to inspire scholars and historians today.
